summary: James and John, with their mother, ask Jesus for the places at His right and left; He speaks of His cup and teaches that greatness means serving.
key_insight: They asked for the places at His right hand and His left in His glory. Within days the places at His right and left were filled, on crosses, by two robbers (Mark 15:27). They did not know what they were asking.
story: Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to Jesus with her sons, kneeling down and asking something from Him. {Mt} James and John said, “Teacher, we want You to do for us whatever we ask.” {Mk}

Jesus asked her, “What do you wish?” She said, “Grant that these two sons of mine may sit, one on Your right hand and the other on the left, in Your kingdom.” {Mt} Mark gives the request in the brothers’ own words: “Grant us that we may sit, one on Your right hand and the other on Your left, in Your glory.” {Mk}
Jesus answered, “You do not know what you ask. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?” {Mk} “We are able,” they said.

“You will indeed drink the cup that I drink, and with the baptism I am baptized with you will be baptized,” {Mk} Jesus told them, “but to sit on My right hand and on My left is not Mine to give, but it is for those for whom it is prepared by My Father.” {Mt}

When the other ten heard it, they were greatly displeased with James and John. Jesus called them to Himself. “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those who are great exercise authority over them. Yet it shall not be so among you; but whoever desires to become great among you, let him be your servant.” {Mt} “And whoever of you desires to be first shall be slave of all.” {Mk}
“For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life a ransom for many.”
differences: Matthew says their mother came with them, knelt and made the request; in Mark, James and John make it themselves.
Matthew has “in Your kingdom”; Mark has “in Your glory.”
Matthew adds that the places are prepared “by My Father.”
Mark says the one who would be first must be “slave of all”; Matthew says “your slave.”

fit.question: Matthew says the mother of James and John asked for the seats. Mark says the brothers asked. Who made the request?

points.label: She came with them
points.text: Matthew says she came “with her sons” and knelt to ask “something from Him.” The request was theirs as much as hers. Mark simply tells it as theirs.

points.label: Jesus answers the brothers
points.text: In both Gospels Jesus turns from the request to the two men: “Are you able to drink the cup?” In Matthew too, it is the brothers who answer, “We are able,” and the ten are angry with “the two brothers.”

fit.note: Matthew includes the mother who spoke for her sons; Mark keeps the focus on the men who wanted the thrones. Both are true.
fit.short: She came with her sons and spoke for them; in both Gospels Jesus answers the brothers. Mark tells the request as theirs.

scene.label: Right hand and left
scene.text: The seats beside a king’s throne belonged to those nearest his power. Solomon set a throne for his mother at his right hand (1 Kings 2:19), and the LORD says to David’s Lord, “Sit at My right hand” (Psalm 110:1).

scene.label: Their mother
scene.text: Matthew 27:56 and Mark 15:40, read side by side, suggest her name was Salome. She was one of the women who followed Jesus from Galilee and later watched at the cross.

scene.label: The cup
scene.text: In the prophets the cup often stands for God’s judgment poured out: “the cup of His fury” (Isaiah 51:17). In Gethsemane Jesus will ask the Father to take this cup from Him (Mark 14:36).

scene.label: They did drink it
scene.text: James was the first of the Twelve to die for Christ, killed with the sword by King Herod Agrippa (Acts 12:1–2). Early church tradition says John lived to old age; he was on Patmos “for the word of God” (Revelation 1:9), most likely as an exile.

scene.label: A ransom
scene.text: A ransom was the price paid to free a slave or a captive. Jesus’ words echo Isaiah’s Servant, who “bore the sin of many” (Isaiah 53:12).

witnesses.matthew: Includes the mother kneeling before Jesus, and has Jesus say the places are prepared “by My Father.” In Matthew the request comes soon after Jesus’ promise of twelve thrones (19:28), and it reads against that promise.
witnesses.mark: Tells the request bluntly, from the brothers’ own mouths, right after Jesus’ fullest prediction of His death. Many see verse 45 as the key to Mark’s whole Gospel: the Son of Man came to serve and to give His life a ransom for many.

seeing.reveals: Jesus does not simply scold ambition; He redirects it. He measures greatness by Himself: the Son of Man who came to serve and to pay with His own life the ransom for many.
seeing.living: Wanting to be great is not condemned; wanting it the way the rulers of the Gentiles want it is. In Jesus’ church the one who serves without being noticed is the one most like Him, and the ransom He paid is the reason.
seeing.ponder: Where are you asking Jesus for a seat when He is offering you His cup?

preaching.big_idea: The Son of Man came to serve and give His life; greatness in His kingdom looks the same.
outline: A cup they did not understand (38–40)
The Servant who pays the ransom (45)
preaching.watch_for: The ten are “greatly displeased” with the two (v. 41), but Jesus’ answer is for all twelve; none of them yet thinks like the Son of Man. Verse 45 grounds the call to serve in the cross itself.
related_other: Isaiah 53:10–12 · The Servant bears the sin of many
Acts 12:1–2 · James killed with the sword
